You yourself said to court a woman!
So that's what I'm doing.
You would do better to wash the dishes at home.

meanings.note: От болезни = from an illness. Common feminine noun meaning 'illness, disease, sickness' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он умер здесь от болезни печени.
examples.trans: He died right here of liver disease.
After his illness he rested for a long time.
That means the disease is progressing!

meanings.note: Intransitive reflexive verb. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fight, struggle', paired with 'побороться'.

examples.trans: He is struggling with his doubts.

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

вести.gloss: to lead, to conduct (вести себя = to behave)

meanings.en: to lead, to guide, to drive
meanings.note: Unidirectional verb of motion. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lead, to conduct (вести себя = to behave)', paired with 'повести'.

meanings.en: вести себя: to behave, to conduct oneself
meanings.note: Вы как маленькая себя ведёте = You're behaving like a little girl

examples.trans: You're behaving like a little girl.

examples.text: Лидия Алексеевна, успокойтесь, пожалуйста! Вы как маленькая себя ведёте.
examples.trans: Lydia Alexeyevna, calm down, please! You're behaving like a little girl.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
For emphasis. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').
Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

добиваться.gloss: to strive for, to seek, to court

meanings.en: to court, to seek someone's favour
meanings.note: + genitive. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'биваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to strive for, to seek, to court', paired with 'добиться'.

examples.trans: You yourself said to court a woman!

meanings.note: Location; compare домой = homeward. Core Russian adv meaning 'at home' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The main thing is, you keep him at home.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

meanings.note: Theatrical or cinematic genre. Common feminine noun meaning 'drama' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The film's genre is heavy drama.

examples.text: Шеф, у меня случилась страшная драма.
examples.trans: Chef, a terrible drama happened to me.

meanings.note: Category of artistic composition. Common masculine noun meaning 'genre' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The film's genre is heavy drama.
The town's mayor, Arkady Anikeev, has been detained.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Something that happened. Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'тория'). Common feminine noun meaning 'history; story' in everyday Russian.
Something that happened. Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'тория'). Common feminine noun meaning 'history; story' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: declines like какой: какая-то, какое-то, какие-то

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Film theater or cinematic art. Common neuter noun meaning 'cinema, movies, film' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Then invite me to the movies.
So, let's look at the schedule in the cinema.

examples.text: Зачем ты вообще ведёшь её в кино?
examples.trans: Why are you even taking her to the movies?

meanings.note: Humorous play or film. Common feminine noun meaning 'comedy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Oh, here is a new comedy!
It is a cheerful comedy about love.
Alright, we will go to this comedy.

meanings.note: Comparative of хорошо. Core Russian adv meaning 'better' in everyday speech.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, little').
colloquial term for something gloomy

examples.trans: Kind of a downer, won't do.

examples.text: Давай выключим эту песню, сплошной мрачняк.
examples.trans: Let's turn off this song, it's total gloom.

meanings.note: Parenthetical adverb. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.
With не / нет. Core Russian det meaning 'no ... at all, not any' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Её, ей, ей, о ней. Core Russian pron meaning 'she; it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: animate masculine noun with fleeting о

examples.trans: You are behaving like a teenager!
The teenagers were walking in the courtyard.

examples.text: Вы ведёте себя как подросток! Вы приударяете за мной.
examples.trans: You are behaving like a teenager! You are flirting with me.

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Completed: the job gets done. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wash', paired with 'мыть'.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: One completed look. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: dishes, plates and cups, tableware (collective singular)
meanings.note: Мыть посуду = to wash the dishes. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'суда'). Common feminine noun meaning 'dishes, tableware, crockery' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Get up and go wash the dishes!
Clean tableware is on the table.

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

meanings.note: Arduous path. Common masculine noun meaning 'path, way, journey' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here is a movie: A Thorny Path.

examples.text: Давай, счастливого пути и хорошей дороги!
examples.trans: Go ahead, safe travels and have a good road!

examples.text: Ты сам выбрал этот страшный путь.
examples.trans: You chose this terrible path yourself.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: List of times of events or films. Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'писание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'schedule, timetable' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: So, let's look at the schedule in the cinema.
The train arrived right on schedule.

meanings.note: рассказывай! = tell me (your news)!

examples.trans: So, tell me, how are you doing?

meanings.note: Romantic mood or feeling. Common feminine noun meaning 'romance, romantic atmosphere' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There is no romance in it at all!

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Тебе смешно = you find it funny. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мешно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мешно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Beset with thorns or difficulties. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('thorny, arduous').

examples.trans: Here is a movie: A Thorny Path.

examples.text: Путь к успеху часто бывает долгим и тернистым.
examples.trans: The path to success is often long and thorny.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: in weight, or тяжёлый металл = heavy metal
Тяжёлый день = a hard day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('heavy; hard, difficult').

examples.text: Я вообще в школе тяжёлый металл любила!
examples.trans: In school I actually loved heavy metal!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'movie, film' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я всегда смотрел фильмы про войну.
examples.trans: I always watched movies about the war.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
